classification.difficultyReason: The hardest parts combine logarithms into a quadratic, solve for irrational roots, and compare each root against simultaneous restrictions on the original arguments.

answer.worked:
The original domain is $x\ne0$. Convert directly to exponential form to retain both signs.

$$\begin{align*}x^2&=3^2\\x^2&=9\\x&=\pm3\end{align*}$$

Both values satisfy the original equation.

The original argument must be positive: $(x+1)(x+2)>0$, so $x<-2$ or $x>-1$.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+3x+2&=2^1\\x^2+3x&=0\\x(x+3)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }x=-3\end{align*}$$

Both values make the original argument equal to $2$, so both are valid.

answer.short:
$x=0$.

Combine the logarithms; the original domain $x>-1$ excludes the other root, $-3$.
answer.worked:
The original domain requires $x+1>0$ and $x+2>0$, hence $x>-1$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_2\big((x+1)(x+2)\big)&=1\\(x+1)(x+2)&=2\\x^2+3x&=0\\x(x+3)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }x=-3\end{align*}$$

Only $x=0$ satisfies $x>-1$, so the solution is $x=0$.

answer.short:
$x=3$.

Combine the logarithms and retain only the root in the original domain $x>2$.
answer.worked:
The original domain requires $x>0$ and $x-2>0$, hence $x>2$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_3\big(x(x-2)\big)&=1\\x(x-2)&=3\\x^2-2x-3&=0\\(x-3)(x+1)&=0\\x&=3\text{ or }x=-1\end{align*}$$

Only $x=3$ satisfies $x>2$, so the solution is $x=3$.

answer.short:
$x=3$.

The combined equation gives $x=\pm3$; the original domain $x>1$ excludes $-3$.
answer.worked:
The original domain requires $x-1>0$ and $x+1>0$, hence $x>1$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_2\big((x-1)(x+1)\big)&=3\\x^2-1&=8\\x^2&=9\\x&=\pm3\end{align*}$$

Only $x=3$ satisfies $x>1$, so the solution is $x=3$.

answer.short:
$x=\pm1$.

Combine the logarithms; both roots lie in the original domain $-2<x<2$.
answer.worked:
The original domain requires $2-x>0$ and $2+x>0$, hence $-2<x<2$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_3\big((2-x)(2+x)\big)&=1\\4-x^2&=3\\x^2&=1\\x&=\pm1\end{align*}$$

Both roots lie in $-2<x<2$, so both are valid.

answer.short:
$x=-3\pm\sqrt7$.

Combine the logarithms and solve the quadratic; both roots satisfy $-7<x<1$.
answer.worked:
The original domain requires $1-x>0$ and $7+x>0$, hence $-7<x<1$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_3\big((1-x)(7+x)\big)&=2\\(1-x)(7+x)&=9\\x^2+6x+2&=0\\(x+3)^2&=7\\x&=-3\pm\sqrt7\end{align*}$$

Both roots lie in $-7<x<1$, so both are valid.

answer.short:
$x=3-\sqrt5$.

Combine the logarithms; the original domain $x<2$ excludes $3+\sqrt5$.
answer.worked:
The original domain requires $4-x>0$ and $2-x>0$, hence $x<2$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_2\big((4-x)(2-x)\big)&=2\\(4-x)(2-x)&=4\\x^2-6x+4&=0\\(x-3)^2&=5\\x&=3\pm\sqrt5\end{align*}$$

Only $3-\sqrt5$ satisfies $x<2$, so the solution is $x=3-\sqrt5$.
